solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Old hat Arab returned to gamekeeper Liz?

indicators.note: to here means added on after, so the turned word follows
a keeper holds something, so the name for Liz holds the word for game

parts.note: Liz and Beth are both short forms of Elizabeth
a hind is a female deer, hunted as game

indicators.note: returned means the word for Arab is read backwards

parts.note: Arabs are Semitic people, so an Arab is a Semite

explanation.surface: A dated Arab gentleman goes back to a gamekeeper named Liz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gamekeeper' reads as a job, but it splits in two: game is the deer word and keeper is the containment signal around Liz's name. 'returned' turns the Arab word round, giving ETIMES.
explanation.definitionFit: Something old hat is outdated, and being behind the times is the idiom for being out of fashion.

clue.text: Some fat daughters producing tears after complaint

indicators.note: after places the daughter and tearing pieces behind the complaint

parts.note: a beef is slang for a grievance or complaint
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
ripping cloth produces tears (rips), read as tares not teardrops

explanation.surface: Girls start crying after one of them complains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tears' reads as weeping, but here it rhymes with 'cares': ripping makes tears in fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef dripping is the fat that runs from roasting beef, a traditional British cooking fat.

clue.text: Composer reportedly wasted having drained dozen

indicators.note: reportedly signals that a word is said aloud to give the opening sound

parts.note: wasted is slang for high on drugs or drink

indicators.note: drained means the inside letters are emptied out, leaving only the ends

explanation.surface: A composer, said to be wasted, has polished off twelve drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: HIGH spoken matches the opening sound of the composer's name, spelt HAY; drained 'dozen' leaves D and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Haydn was the Austrian classical composer, known as the father of the symphony.

clue.text: End for electrician making circuit safe, or lucky escape

indicators.note: End for points to the final letter of the word electrician

parts.note: earthing connects a circuit to the ground for safety

explanation.surface: An electrician finishes the job, making a circuit safe, and narrowly avoids a shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'earthing' is the British term for what Americans call grounding a circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A near thing is a close shave, something that very nearly went wrong.

clue.text: Time without work for such tabloid models?

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work
less means lacking, as in penniless

explanation.surface: A wry question about the time off and lack of work enjoyed by glamour models.
explanation.walkthrough: Page Three models in British tabloids such as The Sun famously posed with no top on.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamour models in British tabloids were often pictured topless, wearing nothing above the waist.

clue.text: Good-natured question taken in EU on revolutionary island

indicators.note: taken in means the question letter is held inside the letters EU
revolutionary means turned round, so the island is read backwards

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile

explanation.surface: A calm question is raised in the European Union about a revolution on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' with Elba nods at Napoleon, but it only signals reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Equable describes a placid, even-tempered person who is not easily upset.

clue.text: Tees is a good one to dismiss over scan result

parts.note: Tees is the setter, so from his point of view this is I am, shortened to I'm

indicators.note: to dismiss means a word is removed from another

parts.note: taken as written
on can mean over, as in a lid on a box

explanation.surface: The setter claims to be a fine fellow to send away after looking over a medical scan.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's own name stands for I'M. Dismissing ON from ONE leaves E.
explanation.definitionFit: A scan, such as an X-ray or MRI, produces a picture of the inside of the body.

clue.text: Reshaped clue concept new and relevant to one geometer

indicators.note: reshaped tells us the letters of clue are rearranged

parts.note: an idea is a concept

explanation.surface: A setter recasts a clue around a new concept connected with geometry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one geometer' is a specific person, Euclid, not geometers in general.
explanation.definitionFit: Euclidean refers to Euclid, the Greek mathematician whose Elements founded classical geometry.

clue.text: Society may conceal word origins

indicators.note: conceal says the letters are concealed inside the run Society may

explanation.surface: Polite society might hide where its words come from.
explanation.definitionFit: Etyma is the plural of etymon, the root form from which a later word derives.

clue.text: Learner in place with cunning Platonist

indicators.note: in means the learner letter sits inside the word for place

parts.note: to put something is to place it
L is a learner, from L-plates on British learner drivers' cars
arch means sly or knowingly cunning

explanation.surface: A student positioned with a clever Platonic philosopher.
explanation.definitionFit: Plutarch, the Greek biographer and essayist, was a Middle Platonist philosopher and priest at Delphi.

clue.text: Wild military pack frog with two heads destroyed

indicators.note: destroyed means the letters of these words are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A savage army pack destroys a two-headed frog.
explanation.definitionFit: The dogs of war, from Julius Caesar, are the savagery of warfare and, by extension, mercenaries.

clue.text: Meals alcove described at first in letter's content

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of described
content means the inside of the word, with its outer letters removed

parts.note: the word letter, whose inside is wanted

explanation.surface: A dining nook is mentioned early in what a letter contains.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinette is a small area or alcove set aside for eating meals.

clue.text: Opener from Buddy Miles rocked hot spot

indicators.note: Opener from takes the first letter of Buddy
rocked means shaken up, so the letters of Miles are rearranged

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Buddy Miles, the rock drummer, opens with a hot spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Buddy Miles was an American rock drummer who played with Jimi Hendrix; 'rocked' fits the music but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A blemish is a spot or mark on the skin or a surface.

clue.text: One's married man abroad for porcelain

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I; the possessive is a link
mari is the French word for husband

explanation.surface: Someone's husband abroad collects porcelain.
explanation.definitionFit: Imari is Japanese porcelain, richly decorated, exported from the port of Imari.

clue.text: Turn up in Scots island church — that shows hubris

indicators.note: in places the turned piece within the island's name

parts.note: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in a game
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Turning up at a church on a Scottish island shows pride.
explanation.definitionFit: Hubris is excessive pride or self-confidence, which is what arrogance amounts to.

clue.text: Person in van Parsee had written off

indicators.note: written off means wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A Parsi man's vehicle has been written off in a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'van' here is short for vanguard, the front of an army, not a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A spearhead is the person or group leading an attack or movement, in the vanguard.

clue.text: Superb setting for river and summit in alpine Arcadia

indicators.note: a setting holds a jewel, so the word for superb holds the river

parts.note: rare can mean excellent, as in a rare treat
the Ural is a river in Russia and Kazakhstan

indicators.note: summit in points to the top letter of alpine, its first in a down clue

explanation.surface: A river and a mountain peak make a fine setting in an idyllic alpine landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcadia is a byword for pastoral countryside, an idealised piece of rustic land.

clue.text: Soothing pride fills last Henrician wife in charge

indicators.note: fills means the pride word goes inside the queen's surname

parts.note: Catherine Parr was the sixth and last wife of Henry VIII
ego is self-esteem or pride

explanation.surface: Henry VIII's last wife, proud and in control, offers a calming presence.
explanation.definitionFit: Paregoric is an old opium-based medicine taken to calm coughs and diarrhoea, hence soothing.

clue.text: Say Capone breaking rule's put straight again

indicators.note: breaking means the gangster's name splits the rule word open

parts.note: to reign is to rule
Al Capone was the Chicago gangster, so Capone gives Al, with say marking an example

explanation.surface: Al Capone breaks the rules and goes straight again.
explanation.definitionFit: To realign is to bring back into a straight line or correct position.

clue.text: When lying in state requires shroud

indicators.note: lying in means the word for when rests inside the state

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California
once means when, as in once he arrives

explanation.surface: When a body lies in state, it needs a burial shroud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lying in state' suggests a funeral, but 'state' is California.
explanation.definitionFit: To shroud something is to hide it from view, a verb meaning to cover or hide.

clue.text: Irish deny female in outfit's not hot

indicators.note: not means the hot letter is taken away
in places the female bird inside the outfit word

parts.note: a rig is an outfit of clothes
a hen is a female bird

explanation.surface: An Irish woman refuses to wear an outfit that isn't hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'female' is a female bird here; with it inside the outfit word you get RHENIG, and 'not hot' takes away its H. The answer is a rare dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: Renig is an Irish dialect form of renege, to go back on or deny.

clue.text: River spirit comes to West Country

indicators.note: comes to West means the pair is read leftwards, from east to west

parts.note: the Aire is a river in Yorkshire
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A river spirit travels to the West Country of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West Country' looks like the region of south-west England; 'West' signals the reversal and 'Country' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigeria is a West African country, the most populous on the continent.

clue.text: Money one may charge unwary tourist?

definitions.meaning: a safari animal that may charge at a careless visitor, as a fleecing trader might

explanation.definitionFit: Rhino is old slang for cash, and the rhinoceros is the beast known for charging.

clue.text: Lotus going to carry British drug-smuggler about

indicators.note: about means everything is turned round and read backwards
to carry means the word for going holds the other pieces

parts.note: on means working or going, as of a machine
a mule is a courier who smuggles drugs

explanation.surface: A British drug courier is carried off over the lotus fields.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelumbo is the botanical genus of the sacred lotus.

clue.text: Picked up intelligence with bombs planted

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word for intelligence is spoken

parts.note: mind means intellect or intelligence

explanation.surface: Spies picked up intelligence that bombs had been laid.
explanation.definitionFit: Mined ground has explosive mines buried in it, ready to go off.

clue.text: Keen as surgeons can be?

parts.note: sharp-witted, and also cutting like a surgeon's knife making incisions

explanation.surface: How eager surgeons can be.
explanation.definitionFit: Incisive means mentally sharp or penetrating, and literally cutting, as surgeons do.

clue.text: Transform Scots town priest leaves

indicators.note: leaves means the priest departs from the town's name

parts.note: Renfrew is a town near Glasgow
Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest

explanation.surface: A Scottish town changes when its priest moves away.
explanation.definitionFit: To renew something is to make it new again, restoring or transforming it.

clue.text: Bird inserts a key given by rowing-club lovers

indicators.note: inserts means the bird takes the letter in among its own

parts.note: a heron is a wading bird
D is a musical key
Leander Club is the famous rowing club at Henley-on-Thames

explanation.surface: A bird bearing a key is presented by the members of a rowing club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given by' sets the rowing-club name after the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Hero was a priestess and Leander her lover, who swam the Hellespont nightly to her.
